correctness.rationale: Connectedness and full dimension follow from r=n-k-1>=1. With x_0=0, the dual-root lattice becomes Z^(n-1). Range<=m gives (m+1)^n-m^n. If the range exceeds m, its extreme pair is a nonedge and must contain vertex 0. For maximum m+h>m, every core coordinate is an arbitrary element of [h,m], while non-neighbor coordinates are arbitrary elements of [h,m+h] with maximum m+h, giving (m-h+1)^r ((m+1)^k-m^k); conversely these choices obey all edges. Unique h and sign prevent double counting. The quotient-root Euclidean Gram determinant is 1/n; Ehrhart leading terms yield volume (n+2k/(n-k))/sqrt(n). Independently counting missing-match extreme pairs gives its comparator. Binomial expansion and s<=m prove the strict all-dilation bound. 32 independent finite enumeration profiles, 45 exact numerator/leading profiles, 175 finite comparison profiles and six independent hull checks passed. Finite checks do not replace the proof.

Their inspected statements do not evaluate a star of deleted edges in K_n or the resulting strict comparison for all Ehrhart dilations. value.rationale: An infinite, naturally defined dense chordal two-clique-gluing graph family has an unknown evaluated polar Ehrhart polynomial; the exact formula is a geometric invariant for every dilation and yields exact Euclidean volume. The missing-star interaction is multiplicative rather than independent additive behavior of deleted matching edges. Strict domination of the matching configuration at every m>=1 and in volume quantifies the role of edge clustering at a fixed deletion budget, a mathematically motivated comparison not deducible from the matching result alone. No universal extremal theorem or unsupported h-star positivity is asserted.
